# ci_lab unit tests

Coverage tests for `ci_lab`, one UT Assert runner per source file, the way
other cFS apps are tested. The tests, their mocks and their build glue were
**generated by [covmock](https://github.com/thesamprice/covmock)** from
coverage and static analysis; nothing under `covmock/` was written by hand.

| file | lines | branches |
|---|---|---|
| `ci_lab_cmds.c` | 17/17 100% | — |
| `ci_lab_app.c` | 66/80 82.5% | 24/34 70.6% |
| `ci_lab_passthru_decode.c` | 15/24 62.5% | 2/6 33.3% |
| `ci_lab_dispatch.c` | 15/46 32.6% | 2/17 11.8% |
| **total** | **113/167 67.7%** | **28/57 49.1%** |

Measured on cFS Draco v7.0.1 (this branch's base), GCC 12, native build. 15
cases, 28 assertions, all passing. How this was produced, and why it stops at
67.7%, is the
[case study](https://github.com/thesamprice/covmock/blob/docs/cfs-ci-lab-case-study/docs/case-study-cfs-ci-lab.md).

## Running them

Nothing here needs covmock. In a cFS tree with this app at `apps/ci_lab` --
for example the cFS quick-start layout, which lists ci_lab on `cpu1`:

```sh
cp cfe/cmake/Makefile.sample Makefile && cp -r cfe/cmake/sample_defs sample_defs
make SIMULATION=native ENABLE_UNIT_TESTS=true prep
make -C build/native/default_cpu1 \
  coverage-ci_lab-ci_lab_app-testrunner coverage-ci_lab-ci_lab_cmds-testrunner \
  coverage-ci_lab-ci_lab_dispatch-testrunner coverage-ci_lab-ci_lab_passthru_decode-testrunner
(cd build/native/default_cpu1 && ctest -R coverage-ci_lab)
```

(`build/native/default_cpu1` is the usual location; your mission's build
directory and target name may differ.)

## What is here

| path | what it is | written by |
|---|---|---|
| `covmock/<unit>/tests/` | UT Assert cases, one file per function under test | covmock |
| `covmock/<unit>/mocks/` | stubs for every function the unit calls that nothing else stubs -- ci_lab's other source files -- plus output-parameter handlers (`--link-closure`) | covmock |
| `covmock/<unit>/covmock.cmake` | attaches the above to the runner (`covmock_add_to_target`) | covmock |
| `covmock/<unit>/manifest.json` | traceability: each case, its coverage gap, its review state | covmock |
| `support/<unit>_setup.c` | each runner's `UtTest_Setup` | `support/make_setup.sh`, from the manifest |
| `support/ci_lab_global.c` | `CI_LAB_Global` for runners that do not compile `ci_lab_app.c` | hand |
| `annotations/*.toml` | `covmock:test` specifications: the intent coverage cannot supply | hand |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | the runners; optionally seeds covmock's configuration. No stub library: each runner's stubs are covmock's | hand |

The annotations are the only hand-written test input: what each case calls,
what its stubs return, and what it asserts. They are deliberately a
placeholder — the case study maps each one to the covmock issue that would let
the tool derive it instead.

## Regenerating

Everything under `covmock/` is disposable and is rewritten, from a 0% baseline
report, by the case study's `ci-lab-case-study.sh round` (see covmock's
`examples/cfs-ci-lab/`). Edit an annotation, rerun it; do not edit generated
files.
